name: CRM Checklist
description: A checklist for setting up and maintaining a CRM with clean data, clear stages, automation and adoption.

items.text: Define the core objects you track — leads, contacts, accounts and deals.
Choose required fields and keep them minimal to protect adoption.
items.note: Every required field is a tax on the rep entering it.

items.text: Standardize picklists for industry, source, status and region.
Set naming conventions for accounts, deals and records.
Document what each field means and who owns it.
Import existing data and map every field to the right place.
Find and merge duplicate contacts and accounts.
Fill or flag records with missing critical information.
Archive or update stale records on a regular cadence.
items.note: Schedule a recurring cleanup so decay never piles up.

items.text: Set validation rules to keep new entries consistent.
Define pipeline stages that match how deals actually progress.
Write clear exit criteria for moving a deal to the next stage.
Set default probabilities and expected close dates per stage.
Define what counts as won, lost and disqualified.
Confirm the whole team agrees on stage definitions.
items.note: Shared definitions make the forecast trustworthy.

items.text: Link contacts to the correct accounts and deals.
Capture roles, decision-makers and relationship strength.
Log key activities — calls, emails and meetings — consistently.
Record communication preferences and consent where required.
Keep a single source of truth so no contact is duplicated.
Connect email, calendar and marketing tools to the CRM.
Automate data capture to reduce manual entry for reps.
Set up lead routing and assignment rules.
Create task reminders and follow-up triggers for each stage.
Test every workflow before rolling it out to the team.
items.note: One broken automation can quietly corrupt data for weeks.

items.text: Build dashboards for pipeline, forecast and activity.
Define the metrics leadership reviews and how often.
Train the team on the agreed process and why it matters.
Monitor adoption and coach reps who fall behind on data entry.
Review the CRM setup periodically and refine fields and stages.
items.note: Treat the CRM as a living system, not a one-time setup.

faq.a: It is a list of tasks for setting up and maintaining a CRM — covering data fields and hygiene, pipeline stages, contacts, automation, reporting and adoption — so the system stays clean, trusted and useful over time.

faq.q: How often should I run the CRM maintenance steps?
faq.a: Run the setup sections once at implementation. Revisit the data hygiene and reporting sections monthly or quarterly so records stay fresh and forecasts stay accurate as the team grows.

faq.q: Why does CRM data hygiene matter so much?
faq.a: Dirty data breaks everything downstream — forecasts, automation and reporting all rely on clean records. Duplicates, blanks and stale fields erode trust until reps stop using the CRM altogether.

faq.q: Can I print this checklist or download it as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. The checklist prints cleanly on one page and downloads as a PDF, so CRM admins can keep it with their setup notes and share a consistent reference with sales and operations.

faq.q: How do I improve CRM adoption with this checklist?
faq.a: Keep required fields minimal, automate data entry where you can, train the team on the agreed process, and tie reporting to the data reps enter, then save the standards as a shared PDF.
